senses.sense_definition: The practice of lending money at exorbitant or illegal rates of interest.

examples.text: The local loan shark was arrested and charged with <w>usury</w> after charging desperate families double-digit weekly interest.
Many countries have strict laws against <w>usury</w> to protect vulnerable consumers from predatory lenders.

senses.sense_definition: An exorbitant or illegally high rate of interest.

examples.text: The interest rate on that credit card is so high that it borders on outright <w>usury</w>.
He was shocked to find that the small loan carried a rate of <w>usury</w> that would make repayment impossible.

senses.sense_definition: The practice of lending money at any rate of interest, historically considered sinful or illegal.

examples.text: In medieval Europe, traditional religious doctrines strictly forbade <w>usury</w> in any form.
Philosophers debated whether charging interest on loans, or <w>usury</w>, was inherently unnatural.

traits.comment: Historically used to refer to any lending at interest, whereas modern usage implies exorbitant rates.

senses.sense_definition: An increase, profit, or return on an investment or endeavor.

examples.text: She hoped her hard work would yield a rich <w>usury</w> of knowledge and experience.
The explorer promised to return the investment with great fame and <w>usury</w>.

traits.comment: Used in a figurative sense of profit or return.
